outputs.justify_why_test_is_missing: The panel shows quantitative bar graphs (cell death % with error bars, n=3). The caption only states Mean ± s.d. and gives no p-values or description of any statistical test. A statistical test should be reported to support claims of differences between conditions (e.g., EGFP-HIPK2 vs control, with/without Flag-MeCP2). The test type (t‑test, ANOVA), whether comparisons are paired or unpaired, one- or two‑tailed, and any multiple-comparison correction should be specified. With only three independent experiments, exact p-values and test assumptions (normality) are particularly important.

The panel contains a quantitative bar graph (cell death % with error bars) but the caption does not report any statistical test or p-values—only Mean ± s.d. A statistical test is needed to demonstrate that observed differences between conditions (e.g., EGFP-HIPK2, K221R, with/without Flag-MeCP2) are significant. The authors should state which test was used, whether comparisons were independent or paired, and how multiple comparisons were handled.

This panel shows multiple group comparisons across time points (24, 48, 72 h) and genotypes (Mecp2-wt vs Mecp2-null). The caption only gives Mean ± s.d. for three experiments and does not describe any statistical test. Appropriate statistical analysis (for example two‑way ANOVA to test effects of time and treatment/genotype, with post-hoc tests) should be reported, including test name, factors, corrections for multiple comparisons, and exact p-values. Without this, claims about differences over time or between genotypes are not supported.

The panel shows quantitative comparisons of cell death across several conditions/genotypes (including rescue and mutant constructs) with Mean ± s.d. reported but no statistical test described in the caption. A statistical test (e.g., ANOVA with appropriate post-hoc comparisons or specific pairwise tests with correction) should be provided to justify claims of significant differences between groups; the caption should state the exact test, whether comparisons are paired/unpaired, tailing, and any multiple-comparison adjustments.
